title: Ohio Value-Add Portfolio I
lede: Two Southwest Ohio assets, 50 units, one construction team. A stabilized value-add apartment community in Cincinnati and a 24-unit adaptive-reuse conversion in Dayton — bought on what they produce, not on what a future buyer might pay.

assets.name: Dana Heights
assets.body: A 1968 garden-style community owned and self-managed by the same private owner for decades. Rents have never been pushed on turn, utilities are not billed back, and expenses have never been professionally tendered. The renovation is a turn-based interior program, so the asset produces income throughout.

assets.name: 434 W Grand Avenue
assets.body: A 1925 building being converted to residential dwelling units. Value here is created through entitlement and construction rather than rent growth. A parking variance is in process with the City of Dayton; closing on the site is conditioned on that relief being granted.

disclosure: Every figure shown is prepared to demonstrate the offering's structure and underwriting method. It is not derived from executed purchase agreements, third-party appraisals or lender commitments. Neither asset is owned by the Company. Targets are hypothetical and are not a prediction or guarantee of results.
